title: Cohort Regression Beacon + Fallback Controller for Canary and A/B Flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight, production-safe 'Cohort Regression Beacon' service paired with a Fallback Controller that enforces automated rollback or traffic diversion for canary and A/B rollouts when model/config changes introduce quality regressions. The beacon continuously evaluates sampled requests across cohorts using curated prompt sets and lightweight metrics (n-gram overlap, toxicity heuristics, length distribution, task-specific score proxies). The controller consumes beacon signals + system health signals and applies escalation policies: gradual pause, divert-to-stable, or full revert. Design must prioritize low false-positive rate, fast detection (~5-15min), and clear audit trail for postmortems.
background: We've seen intermittent regressions from model variant swaps and config tweaks that standard telemetry (latency/errors) doesn't catch. Existing eval-gate work covers large-scale canaries but is heavyweight and slow to iterate. This ticket proposes a focused detection path optimized for quick behavioral regressions tied to changes in generation behavior and safety categories. The goal is a single cross-team tool that product, infra, and SRE can rely on for early rollback decisions without manual intervention.
goals: Detect cohort-level regressions within 15 minutes of traffic exposure
Automate safe fallback to previous stable variant or divert percentage of traffic
Provide per-detection evidence bundles for audits and reviews
Minimize false positives via multi-signal confirmation and hysteresis
non_goals: Run expensive human-in-the-loop evaluations as part of the fast path
success_criteria: End-to-end detection + automated fallback executed in staging and one customer pod in production during rollout test
False positive rate < 2% for monitored cohorts during 2-week A/B sweep
Actionable audit logs and PR link generated for each automatic fallback
design_summary: Architecture: small Beacon service that samples per-route traffic and computes lightweight proxies (per-route score diffs vs baseline, safety flag rates, entropy shifts). Beacon writes compact evidence events to kafka. Fallback Controller runs as a control-plane process that consumes events, applies configured gates (thresholds, confirmation windows, minimum sample counts, dependency checks), and triggers rollout actions via the existing rollout API (pause, scale-down variant, route-shift). Operators can define policies per project/route in a declarative policy file stored in config service. Observability: dashboards for signal trends, and an incident timeline generator that attaches evidence (sampled prompts/outputs, metric deltas, stack snapshots).
signal_definitions: quality_delta: delta of model-specific lightweight score (0-1) aggregated per cohort
safety_flag_rate: fraction of responses triggering safety heuristics
semantic_entropy_shift: distributional change in token entropy compared to baseline
broken_format_rate: fraction of responses failing structured-output parsers
user_error_rate: downstream error events (e.g., parser exceptions) tied to route
policy_schema: thresholds: map-like encoded as strings (quality_delta,<0.08>; safety_flag_rate,>0.01)
tradeoffs: Lightweight proxies trade fidelity for speed—some subtle failures won't be detected in the fast path
Stricter thresholds reduce missed regressions but increase false positives leading to unnecessary rollbacks
Keeping policy authoring simple reduces flexibility—we favor a small set of composable primitives over full boolean logic for now
implementation_tasks: Beacon: sampling hook in runtime (C++/Rust) + sidecar uploader to beacon service
Beacon: implement three core proxies (quality_delta, safety_flag_rate, entropy_shift)
Eventing: compact proto for evidence events and kafka topic config
Controller: policy evaluator service that deduplicates and confirms signals
Controller: integration with rollout API (pause/divert/revert) and write audit event
Console: per-rollout timeline view and one-click override/acknowledge
E2E: synthetic canary tests and chaos tests to validate false positive bounds
Docs: policy authoring guide and runbook for on-call
qa_plan: Unit tests for proxies and policy evaluator
Integration tests in staging with traffic replays and injected regressions
Blackbox test that simulates an A/B sweep producing a safety spike and validates fallback executed
Smoke test that exercises audit log creation and PR linking
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary in staging only (1 day) - validate end-to-end flow
Phase 1: Gradual production canary (0.5% traffic, 30m ramp) with beacon enabled and auto-actions disabled (alert-only) - 48h
Phase 2: Enable auto-actions for non-customer-facing internal routes (1% traffic) - 72h
Phase 3: Full production flow with auto-actions allowed and human-in-loop thresholds for customer-impacting routes
security_considerations: Evidence events contain prompt/response samples — must be PII-scrubbed and encrypted at rest
RBAC controls on who can configure auto-actions and who can view raw evidence
KMS-encrypted audit trails and HSM support for disabling auto-actions via emergency key
open_questions: What minimum sample windows do product teams require for low-traffic routes?
Should we prioritize model-side lightweight scores or runtime-side heuristics for quality_delta?
How to expose policy templates in Console without confusing non-expert users?
acceptance_criteria: Beacon running in staging with >=99% uptime for 48h
Controller executed expected auto-divert for injected regression test and produced audit PR link
Documentation and runbook published on Confluence and linked in rollout config
